utterances.text: It is difficult, because the scale of the map is different. I made calculation for this area that I'm just pointing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does -- is there a street marked 53 in this area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 53, 14, 127. Yes, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, for on the map P10 to the east of the Old Town, the witness pointed streets marked 53, 14, and 127. Do you know which part of the town of Dubrovnik is called Vrata Od Ploca?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Vrata Od Ploca in Dubrovnik is situated directly adjacent to the Revelin fortress to the east, marked by number 170 in this map, and that Vrata Od Ploca are on the road which runs directly before the Revelin fortress, and the name of the street is Frano Supilo? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I took Vrata Od Ploca as a potential target, not Ploce in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, in your report or, rather, addendum to your report, in answer to the question 11(c), you did not say the area of Ploce, but, rather, you said very precisely in the area of Vrata Od Ploca. Do you agree that this is what your report says?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I would like to take a look at it. Are we talking about addendum 1 or 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Addendum 1, question 11(c). It speaks about dispersal pattern, Zarkovica firing position, target Ploce, range 300 metres. Mr. Poje, in B/C/S version that's the question 11(c), paragraph 3, and the question is 11(c) on page 1 of your addendum number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in an English version, it's addendum dated 31st of March, page 2A. Mortar -- this is page 2 of the addendum 1, just at the top of page 2 in English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this addendum, after possibly a deflection for the fourth, fifth, and sixth charge, there is a dispersal pattern for specific cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, please listen to my question. Does it say on page 2 of the English version of the addendum dated 31st of March, and on page 1 of the B/C/S version of your addendum, that you have calculated the values vis-a-vis the Vrata Od Ploca or Ploce gate?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, it just says Ploce target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, please look at addendum 1 to your report. Page 1 of addendum 1 to your report.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 1 says -- speaks about theoretical aspects of dispersion pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Page 1 of your addendum to the report, it says: "Based on the foregoing calculations, determine the average dispersion zone for the examples cited below. Determine whether that zone covers parts of the Old Town or the entire Old Town of Dubrovnik or not." Then we have item (a) the mortar position at Zarkovica firing at the Ploce gate area, and (b) the mortar position at Bosanka firing at the Ploce gate area, and (c) the mortar position at Srdj firing at the Ploce gate or Vrata Od Ploca. Is that what it says in answer to the questions asked of you?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the specific questions in front of me, I just have answers to these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have this text before you, Mr. Poje?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have the report. I don't have the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So what does it say on page 1 of the addendum to your report?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the firing position on Zarkovica, target Ploce, firing range 3 -- 2.300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, would you please listen to my question. On page 1 of the addendum to your report, ERN 03540263 -- can you find it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Page 1 of the addendum to your report, addendum 1 dated 31 March 2004. Could you go back, please, Mr. Poje. Look at the top right corner, ERN number is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show him my copy and then give it back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at this page, Mr. Poje. Did you find it, Mr. Poje?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found number 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give the document back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think the problem is he has answers. He doesn't have the questions, the explanation questions. If we can just read it out, or for the record I can -- I will accept that it says "Ploce gate area." Not "Ploce gate," but "Ploce gate area."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, the original of this report says: "In the area of Vrata Ploce, or Ploce gate." This is what it says on page 1 of the addendum. I'm really surprised the witness doesn't have it in front of him. I would like to ask the registry to give the witness the copy of the document that is part of evidence because it seems that the witness's report is different from the exhibit entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, do you have a complete report that you submitted?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And have you found the page that I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I read it from that page of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about page 1 of the addendum of your report. Do you have that or not?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, it does not say anywhere Vrata Od Ploca, Ploce gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody maybe make additions to your report?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, they did not. All the addenda I did myself, and I signed them, and I also made all the changes and initialed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at the report, please. Is this a page of your report? Is that page 1 of the addendum of your report?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does it state there the Ploce gate area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not say that in the report. When I was making the dispersion calculations, I used a map in which the place of the firing position of the mortar unit is drawn east of the Ploce gate, because the position was not drawn near the Ploce gate, but it was indicated to the east. And for that area, for that sector, the sector where the mortar position was drawn, calculated the dispersion pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you did not respond to the request of the Prosecution to calculate the dispersion in the region of the Ploce gate, the potential dispersion in firing at that target; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on what you consider to be the area of the Ploce gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us move on, Mr. Poje. That is all clear. Do you know that the Revelin fortress is a composite part of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is the Ploce gate? Are they immediately in front of the Revelin fortress?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show the witness P159, Prosecution Exhibit P159.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, do you see the mortar position east of the Old City?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take your ruler and measure how far the position is from the eastern walls of the Old City.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five hundred metres, about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly tell us what the distance is between the Tricavla cape and the Sveti Jakov cape. The Sveti Jakov cape, in order that you can orient yourself as to these 500 metres. I withdraw that question. Could you please measure how broad the Old Town is along the east-west axis if the mortar was positioned 500 metres from the Old Town to the east.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: About 400 metres. And from the eastern ramparts of the Old Town to the mortar positions, you claim that the distance is 500 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correction. I have a marking on the ruler, and yesterday when I was using the other map, which was not to scale, that's what I got, but I will recalculate it now. It's about 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please look at that firing position which you say is at 300 metres. I would like to say before that, the witness through whom this map was introduced on the 22nd of April of 2004 - the name of the witness is Negodic - this witness told the Trial Chamber that that was the position of the Lazareti mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I thought he was going to start with distances. Sorry. Withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness, Witness Negodic, said that this was at a distance of 100 to 120 metres east of the Old Town and that the position was Lazareti.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... you're asking one witness to comment on the testimony of another. You can argue one bit of testimony against each other, not ask one witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, you're addressing counsel not the Bench. Mr. Petrovic, can I suggest that you might put to the witness whether the position would be different if the target was located at the distance that you have just mentioned from the gate rather than at 300 metres, without relating that distance back to the evidence of a particular witness, and we can get what you want that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I was just about to do that, but my learned friend interrupted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if the position of this mortar or these mortars is at 100 to 120 metres from the eastern ramparts of the Old Town, does that change the dispersion pattern that you gave in your report for that position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispersion pattern, if the target was in the position that you have just now stated in which the firing distance is increased by about 100 to 150 metres would not considerably affect the size of the dispersion pattern, because the dispersion pattern, depending on the charge and the firing distance, would change approximately from one to one odd-point metre for every 100 metres of distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the firing position was 100 to 150 metres from the Old Town, would the dispersion ellipse then include the eastern part of the Old Town in this specific case?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the ellipse or the semi-ellipse of dispersion, we have to look at the median hit which should go through the centre of the target, meaning that one-half of the dispersion ellipse faces the weapon and the other faces away from the weapon viewing from the centre of the target, I think that in all calculation I calculated that all the semi-axes were up to 100 metres, and I do not rule out the possibility of some undershots, but this would be very, very slight.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we move 200 metres to the west, that means that the axis of dispersion would also move 200 metres to the west. In that case, would the semi-axis include the eastern part of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not, because like I said, the dispersion ellipse depends on the distance, on the firing distance, and it would increase only slightly because of those 200 metres. If we change the distance by 200 metres, the actual dispersion would change by only one or two metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The target, Mr. Poje, has moved 200 metres to the west in relation to your calculation. Please wait till I pose the question. If the target is moved by 200 metres to the west, even if the ellipse itself didn't change, would it not encompass an eastern part of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the average trajectory of the ellipsis would go through the centre of the target, which is in the east of the -- to the town. I said that we had to look at the semi-ellipse, and it would not include the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Poje. Could you please look at this map which is in front of you. From the position that you see here, is -- on this map, and we're talking about positions east to the town, do we have 17 different targets that are noted here going to the south from Dubac through Zarkovica, Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These markings, these squares, do they indicate targets for the firing position on which we are speaking of east of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are possible or eventual targets for which initial firing elements were prepared in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This target east of the Old Town -- this firing position, excuse me, east of the Old Town had the firing prepared in advance, the elements for Zarkovica, Bosanka, and Dubac east of the Old Town;

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about a covered target which you cannot see from the Zarkovica observation point, do you believe that this -- that you could successfully fire at Zarkovica, Bosanka, and Dubac successfully as this was given?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. With indirect firing, fire is directed from the observation post, not from the weapon's location. You can have elements which are calculated to get the target. So the firing is directed from the observation post. It does not have to be -- the post doesn't even have to be close to the firing position. The communications will ensure communication between the firing and the command or the reconnaissance posts. So between the firing executors and the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you use that firing position -- would you use it to act against yourself from Zarkovica, Bosanka, Dubac? Speaking in principle.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that we would do that, generally speaking, because from a tactical point of view, that position is pretty forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that you could -- well, you could hit it pretty easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And how would you fire then at the given targets? Why was it placed there in the first place?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that you cannot fire from those firing positions; you can. But you asked me whether this was a good position in view of the fact that I would be exposed to fire of the other side. Perhaps I wouldn't pick those positions. It's just a question of the situation at the time and whether the terrain can provide cover for the -- for the firing position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about a well-covered firing position which you cannot see from any of the observation posts of the other side, which is in a small park or it's covered by a -- or screened by a large building, would that be an adequate position in such conditions to use it as a firing position and to fire from it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, a firing position must be picked so that it can assure the execution of firing tasks. So that means that you need to pick a location where the obstacles which are around the firing position do not prevent it from operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if it's picked in a way that it is well covered and that the environment does not prevent it from being operational; it's very well covered, cannot be observed from the observation post, it's behind a tall building and can be used for firing, in those circumstances would you use such a position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in those situations -- in that -- in those circumstances, I would. I'm not saying I would or that I wouldn't. It depends on the specific situation. I wasn't there so I don't know. I didn't fire from that position, and I simply -- when somebody decided to place mortars in that position, probably they took into account all of those things that you mentioned, that the position can execute successful fire on the drawn or visible targets. These are possible targets. It doesn't mean that these targets were actually fired at, because in the preparation for operations, we determine in advance the most probable enemy locations and then we calculate the elements for those locations in advance so that very quickly if they are there or nearby, we can open fire as quickly as possible at the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: With all of those assumptions, the person who picked this position, if they had taken into account all of those things, then your answer would be yes? Could you please repeat your answer. It's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of procedure is followed if the target of a mortar goes 3 per cent in or out of the trajectory? What does that imply in terms of the positioning of the mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the direction of the objective is plus/minus 3 per cent, that is to say according to an azimuth which goes beyond the value that you mentioned, then the mortar is moved by moving the bi-pod.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does a significant number of preparations for firing have to be repeated then?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like the first time. Again, the levels have to be adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long does this procedure take?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When crew members are highly trained, then it moves very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say up to three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what about crews that are not trained?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never measured time in that sense, so I don't know how long untrained crew members would take. That's not something that one looks at in principle. One looks at trained personnel only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what about if the position of the base plate is changed?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Anything I'd say would be just off the top of my head, but it's relatively fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Give us an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to say that if we are expected to take long time from a particular firing position, preparations in terms of the surface take place beforehand. I never really measured time, the time that is needed for preparing a surface. We would have a break because a mortar would be moved five or six metres left or right, but to tell you the truth, I don't know how long it would take.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Type of ammunition. You mentioned smoke shells and compact -- contact shells.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to hear your definition. I would like to hear whether you will agree with what I will put to you, and that is to say that incendiary shells are those that are filled with Napalm and other such material. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that such an inflammable shell does not exist for a 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the literature that I have always used and that I am still using, there is no mention for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us just one more thing in relation to that: The difference between the specific temperature of the burning of wood and the burning of dry grass.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must be a difference, but I don't know how big it is. It is much harder to set wood on fire than it is to set dry grass on fire. Now, what temperature is needed I really cannot say. When we used tracers, I remember that we would set it on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We've understood this. Tell us, please, smoke shells, are smokescreens -- they're actually smoke -- smoke shells are used for creating a smokescreen; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it right that a smoke shell is used, for instance, for getting a unit out of a particular area where it is?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the intention of -- we're talking about a movable target. Does it require a greater expenditure of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does it considerably increase the expenditure of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as movable targets are concerned, a special kind of fire is required which can be along one line or several lines, and then firing has to take place along these lines that are calculated beforehand. And there is not a significant increase in ammunition expenditure, because if we are talking about personnel and if the personnel is out in the open, then within the shortest span of time possible, the strongest fire should be effected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned tracer bullets yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's not tracer bullets. Rather, you did not use the right word in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a tracer can be seen only from the position of a person at a firing position, that a tracer cannot be seen from the target?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A tracer can be seen from the emplacement and also from the flanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But not from the target?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle I wouldn't know because nobody ever fired that kind of ammunition in my direction, so I cannot say whether a tracer can be seen from a target. But I am sure that from the flanks it can be seen because usually we do watch targeting from the flanks, don't we, so that's how we can see these tracers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know M42 ZIS 76 millimetre guns?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the intention of this is?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like any other; to neutralise armoured vehicles, bunkers, fortified buildings too, and perhaps even machine-gun nests and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could P132 be placed before the witness again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we look at a ZIS cannon in the area of Uskoplje, we said yesterday that the altitude is about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And if the target engaged is on Srdj, if it is the fort of Srdj at 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In view of the trajectory of the projectile from a ZIS cannon, can you tell us, if the projectile misses Fort Srdj, where is it going to fall? From Uskoplje to Srdj.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm looking at it, but I'm just trying to locate Srdj. It would go north or north-east of the Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mean north-west?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, north-west of the Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That projectile would not fall into town, and it would most probably fall into the sea, in view of its trajectory.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, you made reference to -- just a moment, please. There is reference made to full preparations, shortened preparations, and simple preparations. Why is one or the other or the third type of preparations carried out under certain circumstances?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the accuracy and quantity of information for targeting. So there is either full preparation, shortened preparation, or simple preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When it is necessary to open fire urgently, is there enough time to carry out full preparation? And what are all the things that have to be done in order to carry out full preparation for targeting?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I'm going to answer your first question. Meteorological and ballistic corrections are made beforehand. If we have the appropriate bulletin and if we have the ballistic conditions of targeting that are gathered at the firing position, then the meteorological and ballistic corrections are calculated and the graph of these corrections is drawn, and when the target appears, then its topographical range is established, and then from the graph, according to the topographical elements, we see how big the meteorological ballistic corrections are, and then these corrections are included in topographic elements, and then targeting can start, or firing can start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the target is changed, then all of that you referred to just now has to be done yet again.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but it's not. It's not necessary to do it all again. Meteorological and ballistic corrections are calculated for an area, not for a specific objective or target. This can be calculated in general terms. So that is the pattern also for three directions. So, for example, two ranges, three directions, and then one direction, three ranges. So when the topographical distance or range is determined, it is possible very quickly, within 15 seconds or so, to look at the graph and to see what the meteorological and ballistic corrections are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If there is no meteorological bulletin, what do you do in that situation? If you do not have one, if the unit concerned does not have one?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we do not have a meteorological bulletin, if we do not have the meteorological conditions and data for targeting that were compiled by a meteorological station, then we can start shortened procedure which does not specifically differ in the basic method. However, the meteorological and ballistic corrections for the same directions and the same ranges or distances are calculated on the basis of ballistic elements of targeting, which are usually accessible, and also the meteorological conditions for targeting on the ground.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please stop before the question -- the answer ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When are simple preparations carried out?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we do not use meteorological, ballistic corrections. Then targeting or firing takes place only on the basis of topographical information, and then it is possible to determine the range or distance merely by sight. We simply look at it. May I just finish? Our rules say that if it is possible, then the decrease in initial velocity has to be taken into account because that is in the firing tables. But that does not change things essentially. So I would like to conclude by saying that simple preparations means targeting only with topographical elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. What does -- I mean, we're now going to move on to the firing tables for a 120-millimetre mortar, so could you please look at column 18. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Column 18 is a table correction due to a lateral wind, Vy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the value because of this lateral wind?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: For ten metres per second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Are they referring to the 120-millimetre booklet, table booklet; and if they are, could that be placed on the ELMO so we can all see what they're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we can use the exhibit that my colleague Mr. Weiner tendered yesterday, and I thought that he understood, of course, that that is what this was all about. It is P182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I have that, but on the ELMO is a later page. 106 to 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is for a charge 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm asking about firing tables in principle, in general. The page doesn't matter. The witness explained to us that column 18 is invariably the same, so it really doesn't matter at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's just that we now have Exhibit P182 on the ELMO, and that will minimise confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Table corrections because of lateral wind, in terms of metres per second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, please look at 18 very carefully, column 18. It says correction of direction because of lateral wind, and it says -- and it says in thousandths of a second.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought of the lateral component of wind. The values are in the column. It is 1:6.000, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it is -- we are talking about thousandths?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In all calculations in addendum 1 and addendum 2, when calculating the dispersion ellipsis, did you take into account correction in the direction due to lateral wind, correction of distance because of winds across the length? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account deviations because of temperature, air pressure, and the temperature of gunpowder?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take the firing tables that are before you now and calculate the following for us: One projectile from your example, which from 5.600 metres is fired at a target which is 150 metres away from the Old Town and where there is a lateral wind of 5 to 10 metres per second, how much does that projectile move away from its trajectory? Please take 5.600 into account, 5 to 10 metres per second. Please calculate the deviation of this projectile in terms of its direction from its trajectory?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the sixth charge at a distance of 5.600 metres and if the lateral component of ballistic wind is 10 metres per seconds --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From 5 to 10.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not the same thing. Five is 5 and 10 is 10. For 10 it is 24 thousandths, and obviously it is that in half for 10 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do the calculation on the basis of 10.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 25 thousandths, if we're looking at the lateral wind in terms of the direction, not to complicate matters further.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please calculate the deviation of the projectile in such a situation. Could you please multiply it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 times -- 25 times 5.6, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: 140 metres per direction. Now, could you please look at the deflection of this trajectory under -- with lateral wind coming from the left. In other words, the shell will deviate by 140 metres to the left. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably if the wind is coming from the left then it will turn to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Can we take the same example. If we have a longitudinal wind 10 metres per second, could you please calculate where this projectile will land.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will deviate by 223 metres from the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we have a situation with a changeable wind with different values, what will happen with the dispersion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the dispersion will change, too. Depending on the direction, speeds of the wind, the dispersion pattern will also change.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mean by increasing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the wind is not so strong, then it will decrease. Therefore, the pattern changes given the change in firing conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The dispersal pattern, therefore, increases; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All your calculations were made taking specific conditions for one specific mortar. Tell us, what will happen with the value of dispersion of a projectile in terms of range and direction if at the same time more than one weapons are being fired from?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we use multiple weapons, then we have a complex dispersion pattern, and the space is bigger than the one when you have -- when you are using a single weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that we take now another break, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that would be a good idea, Mr. Petrovic. Perhaps you could assist us with our future planning. How do you see your time at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will need another half a -- Your Honour, I will need another half hour to complete my interrogation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could you please give the witness map P160.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, can you tell us based on which document did you establish that an aircraft gun was at 150 to 200 metres north from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the map, and there was a symbol of an anti-aircraft gun marked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, did you do that based on this map marked P160?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now take your ruler and measure the distance between the top of the arrow to the Old Town wall. What is the distance between the two? I repeat, from the top of the arrow up to the wall, not up to the lower end.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About six millimetres, given the fact that there is no scale indicated on the map and having some knowledge of the area where there's an entrance to the city and a parking lot, I estimate that the distance would be about 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. I asked you according to the map, what is the distance between the top of the arrow and the Old Town wall as the map shows.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How far is the lower end of the arrow since it crosses the wall? So how far is the lower end of the arrow from the wall of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please measure it.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that means that the arrow, the lower -- lower part of the arrow is about 50 metres inside the Old Town. Based on this map, can you tell us, what is the distance between the northern part of the wall of the Old Town and the Adriatic Highway to the north in the direction of Srdj? Can you please measure that.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 28 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much is that in metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the scale on the map, but I can say that it's approximately 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you worked with this map and if there's no scale indicated on it, how did you arrive at the conclusion that this anti-aircraft gun was at 150 metres to the north from the wall of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my estimate. Bearing in mind and knowing a little this region, I just assumed where the gun would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you did not make your estimate based on the map but, rather, based on your assumption which is then again based on your knowledge of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I also used the map. I used this auxiliary ruler, and I made comparison between two maps. One had the scale; the other one didn't. I made this kind of makeshift ruler and I measured the distance. How accurate that is, I cannot say. I said yesterday that symbols in principle just signify the region or the area where the position is, not the exact point of the position. So it's a relative matter whether the distance is 100 or 130 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could that have been 150 metres to the south, in Stradun, if this is just approximate and in principle?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, it could have been anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it could have been 150 metres to the south from the northern wall, in principle, by interpreting the symbols?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was in the area around the symbol, and that's what I took as a basis, the top of the arrow as a kind of benchmark there where the position could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In principle and by construing only the symbol, that could have been either 150 metres to the north from the symbol or, rather, from the wall, and it could have been 150 metres to the south of the wall if you take only a symbol as the benchmark.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if we take the symbol as the only benchmark, and theoretically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be given now the map P10, and I would kindly ask the witness to take the ruler again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, could you please look at the starting point of the cable car leading to Srdj, and it is directly under the letter O of the word "Ploce." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The starting point of the cable car structure directly above the letter O, can you measure the distance between this point and the northern wall of the Old Town? Please, sir, not like that. Put it vertically. Measure it vertically, Mr. Poje.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 130 and 140 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please measure, since you say that the map symbols indicate areas, can you please measure the distance from where it says Ploce as the central part of the area and the northern wall of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see Bogisica Park in this P10 map? Can you see it, Mr. Poje?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which map did you use, Mr. Poje, to calculate the distance between Bogisica Park and the wall?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map that we just saw a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give the witness the other map, and could the witness please keep the first one before him him. Please place the map. Just a little bit to the top so that we can see the Old Town. A little bit further up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, where is Bogisica Park?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And can you please measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-three millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which point did you start your measurement?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From which point did you start?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So from this point that you have just indicated --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of this almost circular road up to the wall is 19 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much is that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, it's between 250 and 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't need the map P10 [as interpreted] any more. Could you please take a look at this map. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: To the east from the area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this crossroad?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from this crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that the record is clear, I think you put aside Exhibit P160 and are now using Exhibit P10. The transcript would suggest the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the eastern part, where it begins, to the walls of the Old Town, could you please measure the distance between those two points.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why twice, once during the examination-in-chief and again today in answer to my questions, you've said that you calculated the values as at the base of the cable car as 300 to 350 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map that I used, which is at a scale of 25.000, it means that one millimetre is 25 metres. The map was a little bit damaged, it was a photocopy, so based on the measurements that I did, I calculated that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you calculate it -- did you measure it correctly now?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably not any more precise than the first or the second time that I did it, because I'm measuring it now for the third or the fourth time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The base of the cable car at 130 to 140 metres, as you measured it now, or is it at 300 to 350 metres as you said during the examination-in-chief? This is a difference of three times as much. One measurement is three times greater than the second one.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the distances average between those. It's the average of those two values, so it's about 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Once you said 130, so this range of the cable car goes from 130 to 350 metres, according to your measurements.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please measure on map P10 the distance from the northern walls of the Old City to the Adriatic Highway using the vertical line from Minceta.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 330 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So according to your calculations today, the Adriatic Highway, which is the last road before Srdj, is 330 metres -- is at 330 metres, while you said to us during the examination-in-chief that the cable is at 330 metres, and according to what you said, the beginning of the cable car is above the Adriatic Highway, Mr. Poje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, your calculations are not correct. Your calculations are so different that it's impossible to determine where the point is from which you are measuring the distance to the Old Town walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. Argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's fair to put that proposition to the witness, and I'll treat it as a proposition being put to the witness, in fairness to you, Mr. Weiner, given what has preceded. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please respond, Mr. Poje.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about Croatian forces, what does the information mean to you that there was just one site for three mortars? What would be the precision of such firing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What does it mean to you if mortars are fired without using a sight device? What would be the precision of such firing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard it being fired from a mortar without using the sighting devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that you've never heard of anything like that, but if I were to claim that -- if I were to tell you that firing was executed without the sighting device, what would you say about the precision of such firing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: For elevation you can take the quadrants. According to the direction, you would probably need to target with the barrel, and such targeting would be very imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I said that the ZIS gun was being fired without a sighting device? What would you say about the precision of such firing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very poor, but this may not be the case if we're talking about direct firing, because if the distance was not very great and the target was in a clearing, then the precision would be higher. However, at larger distances, the precision would be reduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In view of the characteristics of the ZIS gun, if we're talking about a target at 3.500 metres away, what would you say about such firing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: With such a weapon, without a sighting device is something that I would never fire from, because the precision of firing from such a weapon at 3.500 metres from a place from which I do not have direct line of sight of the target is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the ZIS firing position was 300 metres below the target that is being fired at, and if the target is at 3.500 metres, and if the trajectory crosses the Old Town, is there a possibility that the projectile would hit the Old Town area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it depends on where the weapon was located. If it was -- if the town was in the upward part of the trajectory, and even if theoretically crosses above the town, still the chances would be very slight of the projectile hitting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you base that statement on? If you're firing without a sighting device in circumstances or conditions for which you said that you would never fire in, why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the following: Even though I do not have a sighting device, I can take the proper elevation by using a quadrant. The elevation can be determined based on the firing distance. So the firing distance is something that can be quite correctly gauged. We can assume that, and that the elevation is appropriate to that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you don't have anything of the firing equipment, such as a quadrant, if you have nothing, what would you say would be the precision of such firing in such conditions?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's imprecise, and I would never execute such fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the maximum elevation angle is of the ZIS 75 gun?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at the end of this part of the questioning, would it be possible to give two explanations, even though I prepared more, so that some things could be clearer? They refer to the errors in the preparation of initial elements and the dispersion pattern. Also, the impact dispersion if the target is below the horizon of the weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be matters, Mr. Poje, which Mr. Weiner will take into account, and if he thinks it necessary, he will ask questions about them. That's his role now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Colonel Poje, could you please explain those two answers now and then we'll go to some of my questions.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all I would like to try to clarify the size of the dispersion pattern, which we discussed yesterday and today, and the effect of certain elements on the dispersion, impact dispersion. The preparation of initial elements is a phase during which correct firing elements are determined in the shortest possible time in order to start firing and group firing. The initial firing elements contain a relatively large number of errors; accidental errors, systemic errors. I'm ruling out the gross errors. They also contain those errors in the conditions of firing. If we did not take into account the meteorological and ballistical firing conditions in the beginning, then those initial elements would contain those errors. If we did take the meteorological and ballistic errors into account, or corrections into account, then those -- we would rule out those amongst the accidental errors. I would like to also represent what I am saying in a -- in the form of a graph. This represents the target. The line that I am drawing is the azimuth or the direction of fire. Let's assume that the observation point is on the -- along the hypothetical firing-line. This is not always so, but it's possible. The initial -- with the initial elements, we have fired the first projectile. I have marked that first hit with the letter P. From that point onwards, all errors in the meteorological and ballistic conditions of firing are contained in this vector. We establish that vector by reading the deflections by direction, and we also determine the deflection by distance, and that is that P which contains all the errors in the preparation of initial elements. As the firing continues, those errors -- perhaps I should also say that in that vector, errors - and a deflection indicates that there was some error that occurred - we don't know how much of that is accounted for by topographical, ballistic, or meteorological errors, which all have their role in the firing and in the execution of fire. In order to hit the centre of the target, we must perform the appropriate corrections, and the correction, as you can see, has to be made to the right, and it has to be closer. I will mark that with a minus, that correction to the right. In the continued process of firing, we correct the measuring and rounding up errors, and we possibly determine new elements or we use elements that were used before. When I have managed to achieve a median shot into the centre of the target according to the rules of operation, then the dispersion pattern can be increased if the firing conditions from one projectile to the next change substantially. If the firing conditions are relatively the same from one projectile to the next, then the dispersion is usual, it's normal, and it corresponds to the probability theory for dispersion. That means that later, an error in the initial firing speed no longer plays a role, or the lateral or longitudinal winds play a role, because this is already contained in this vector which shows us the degree of the deflection. It does have a role if from one projectile to the next the wind blew at 2 metres per second and then 10 metres per second for the next projectile. I said I didn't know what the circumstances were, the conditions were at that particular time, but this is just a theoretical representation by which I want to say that all the errors which I have named, except some accidental errors or measuring errors, can be ruled out. So once again, this vector would contain the initial velocity and the wind. So if I did not take into account the initial velocity, then the vector would account it. If I did include it, then that would be an initial element -- accidental error in the initial velocity. That would be the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a few questions and we'll get back to your second part. I just want to clarify this. What you're saying is calculations or your ellipses are not based on the initial shots with the errors but they're based on the shots after the adjustments have been made; after the weather and temperature and all those adjustments have been made; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispersion ellipse is determined on the basis of the median shot. The objective of each firing, as a rule, is to have the median hit the centre of the target. It's possible that I did not mention the median -- the first hit in the explanation. The first hit can deflect to a greater or lesser degree, depending on the conditions of firing and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We have very little time and we're trying to finish you up today, and I know the Court wants you to be finished today so they can start a new witness tomorrow. So I only have 20 minutes, so... So once again, the median shot, the ellipses or your median shot, those are based on the shots fired after the corrections have been made?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, sir, you were shown different calculations as -- in relation to distances when you used map P10 and P160. Are these original maps or are those photocopies?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had photocopies of maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are photocopies more difficult to use than originals?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please clarify the time. When did he have these photocopies? I understood the witness to have had the photocopies at the time when he was preparing his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's what his evidence has been just now, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are photocopies more difficult to use than regular -- than original maps?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to work on photocopies. It's more difficult to work with copies than with originals, especially in conditions when the photocopies were made without giving the scale. Then there are certain deviations or distortions that you get, even if you copy on the scale 1:1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the ones that you used in court, are those also photocopies? The maps that you were shown in court.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were photocopies except for the last map. I'm not sure, but I think that I also had photocopies here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to move, sir, to the 120-millimetre mortars. There were a number of questions about 120-millimetre mortars, and yesterday Defence counsel asked you why you used 120-millimetre mortars in your hypotheticals, and Defence counsel told you at page 74 that Admiral Jokic had testified at page 3980 that they had 82-millimetre mortars at the fire support group of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade at Uskoplje. In examining -- I'll -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no. On page 3980, we're talking about the 120-millimetre mortars in Uskoplje. I never said --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For the record, I will read the transcript. On page 3980 of the transcript Admiral Jokic describes the composition of a battalion fire support group, the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, at Uskoplje and gives -- and states there that "as part of the battalion firing group, we have 82-millimetre mortars." That's what you said yesterday. An examination of the transcript reveals that Admiral Jokic did not mention 82-millimetre mortars at that location and that he was discussing the month of November, which you'll notice on page 3975. And I will read what Admiral Jokic says: "However, as regards artillery or, rather, mortars, 120-millimetre mortars that were within the circle, that was the artillery of the 3rd Battalion in the area of Uskoplje. From there, the Old Town could be targeted including the city harbour and part of the New Town of Dubrovnik outside the old walls." Admiral Jokic further testifies -- we can put this on the ELMO if you have any questions, Counsel, and you can read it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You haven't finished, Mr. Weiner, and then I'll hear Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Admiral Jokic further testified about the same position in December of 1991, which they mentioned the December map on page 4011, and on page 4020, Admiral Jokic says the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you discuss those positions and what the symbols mean.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a firing group belonging to the battalion. This is only its short name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of what battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 3rd Battalion. This is the battalion firing group of the 3rd Battalion providing support for other units of the 3rd Battalion. It's 120-millimetre mortar battery containing six mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what is the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were the weapons that you've just discussed in the range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: From that position it is possible to target the Old Town. The range is 6 kilometres and the distance is between 5 and 6 kilometers and that's the edge of the firing range so to speak. My question to you is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. If you'd pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not check yesterday's transcript, so I do not know what was interpreted into English yesterday, but I do know what I said, and I know what my colleague is reading out now is all correct. Yesterday, not at a single point in time did I mention or did I ask whether there were any 82-millimetre mortars at Uskoplje or did I ever claim that 82-millimetre mortars are at Uskoplje. On the contrary. Precisely what my learned friend Mr. Weiner has been saying. It was precisely that. In November and December at Uskoplje there were 120-millimetre mortars. So I would like the witness to say whether I ever mentioned yesterday 82-millimetre mortars at Uskoplje or whether I made any kind of proposition of that kind to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've been thinking now. As far as I can remember, yesterday we only discussed 120-millimetre mortars in the area of Uskoplje and at the command post of the battalion, not other units in the area of Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, do you want to go on with your question based on the transcript, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Based on the transcripts I've just read to you, do you agree with Admiral Jokic's testimony that Uskoplje, with 120-millimetre mortars, is within the firing range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The range of this mortar with a light shell is about 6.400.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So is it within the range of the Old Town, those 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you mean to ask is the Old Town within the range of the mortar at Uskoplje, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll use the Judge's question. Is --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the firing position of the mortar in Uskoplje, it is possible to fire at the Old Town, to target the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, today as well as yesterday -- no. Today you were asked about some of your conclusions to questions 20 and 21 in your first report and as to what could be struck by the 82- and 120-millimetre mortars. And my question is: Did you take into account in that question the additional positions on Srdj and Bosanka mentioned in the supplements and the addendum?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I did, but I did not take the front end into account. I looked at the mortars as if being withdrawn a bit in terms of the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And by including those mortars in Srdj and Bosanka, are those mortars, the 82-millimetre mortars, within the range of the Old Town? I'm sorry, is the Old Town within the range of those mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they are directly at Srdj or if they are on the edge of Bosanka, they do fall within the range of the Old Town. They would be able to reach the Old Town anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you exclude the possibility that there were other weapons not depicted by the symbols on the map?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this particular subject matter, whether there were any other weapons, where they could have been or things like that, I have not dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But can you exclude the possibility that there were no other weapons -- that there were other weapons?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible. It's not that I can claim that it's not possible, but on the basis of the maps I saw, obviously that was not the case, although we mentioned yesterday mortar units, for instance, of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified today that targets are selected in such a way so as to be away -- to be as far away as possible from cultural monuments and humanitarian facilities. What factors must be considered prior to deciding to fire at a target in a civilian populated area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A target is where it is. We cannot change that. What we can change is the point from which we will start firing. In principle, in front of the target, if we look from the weapon. We choose a point which is far away, far enough, and then at the beginning of the firing, we are not going to hit a building that is a cultural building or a housing building or anything like that. So when shooting at targets that are close to such buildings, the beginning of the targeting, the beginning of the corrections due to the mistakes, the errors that I referred to originally, we choose another point from which we start the correction and then, simply, we get closer and closer, and I go all the way to the centre of the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is this precaution used to limit collateral damage?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained a few minutes ago that the preparation of initial elements includes a relatively large number of errors. Accidental, systematic errors due to a lack of consideration for meteorological and ballistic information. We don't know whether that error is going to cause an overreach or a shortfall in terms of the target, but the probability of this is that even if the target is not hit but if there is an overreach, the shell will not fall on the protected building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, if you observe a weapon firing from a building in a populated area where neutralisation would cause heavy or extensive collateral damage to civilian objects, what is the appropriate response, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already answered that question once. First an attempt is made to make sure that there is no firing from that building through some kind of command and control, mutual communication. It should be said that there is firing from a protected building, and if this is not dealt with, then that building will have to be shot at. I think I wrote it in the report. If there is shooting coming from a building, regardless of whether it is protected or not, it should be expected that the enemy is going to target that building in return. Of course, trying to damage it, that is to say the building, as little as possible. So if possible, the kind of weapon that should be used is a high precision one with a very small dispersion, and I would say, if possible, use a weapon for direct firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there was some discussion today about rear slope, and you indicated that there was a mild slope. Could you please explain what you meant by a "mild slope."

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The slope between the Old Town or the ramparts of the Old Town and the Adriatic road is a variegated one. That means that it's a bit hilly. It goes up and down and then up and down. That is to say if we were to draw a tangent from the buildings in the Old Town to the Adriatic road, yes, there is a small, mild slope there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. This does not significantly affect the dispersion pattern. Again, I say that the firing is vertical and the descent angles are very big. That is to say that the effect of the slope on the terrain is not that great. It is always a factor of influence, but not to a very considerable degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, the fact that it's a mild slope in relation to being viewed from Uskoplje, does that also mean that it's a mild slope in relation -- or a mild rear slope in relation to Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague is imprecisely quoting what has been said. It was never said in this courtroom that this target or objective can be seen from Uskoplje. The witness said that several times, that that target cannot be seen from Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about direction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If it is a mild slope from the direction of Uskoplje, does that also mean it's a mild slope from the direction of Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The terrain in the area of the target looked from the point of view of the weapon is the same regardless of whether we observe it from Zarkovica or Srdj or some other location. For the weapon, it's the same thing, if we are talking about the weapon emplacement. At Uskoplje that is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: From Zarkovica, is it a rear slope?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we observe from Zarkovica. Now let us say that the weapons are at Zarkovica and that the observation post is at Zarkovica. Perhaps we could say that it is a mild lateral slope from Uskoplje, a mild rear slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir -- if the Court would give him a minute or so, could he please briefly explain that other issue he had and I'll limit my redirect examination to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You did have a tight time, and there have been interruptions, so if you need a little longer, Mr. Weiner. You're asked, Mr. Poje, about the second matter you wanted to discuss or explain. Do you remember that matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is the dispersion of hits when the target is below the horizon of the weapon. If you give me a minute or two or three, if you permit me, I'll try to deal with it in the briefest possible terms because I've prepared it, and I'm going to use the same graphic tables that we saw yesterday. So I'm not going to take up too much time. What you have before you are the same graphic tables for the sixth charge. Yesterday we talked about 6 kilometre ranges topographically. The topographical distance of the target is actually the horizontal distance from the firing position to the projection of the target C prim, as I have marked it, in terms of the horizon of the weapon. That is the topographic distance of the target. Yesterday we established that if we were to fire a shell that corresponds to this distance, that this is where the impact would be, at P1. That's where it would fall. That is to say there would be an overreach of the target. The point of targeting is not to miss a target but to hit it. That means that I have to find an elevation that will hit point C, not point B1 -- P1, rather. So I have to correct things; correct the distance. And now how much? Yesterday I said it was 230 metres. So by 230 metres. And how can this be seen in terms of the elevation? The cotangent and then the 230 value will give us this correction, when I now find the trajectory that will hit point C. So I tried to improvise it. Here it is. That's the trajectory. We see that actually the distance of targeting at the horizon has been decreased, and we see that the dispersion pattern is decreased with the decrease of this distance. Not too much, either in a positive or in a negative sense. I have already said that at every 100 or 150 metres of the distance, the Vd and Vp are changed 1 or 2 metres which ultimately, if we take into account these 200 metres, as I already mentioned today, would not contribute to a significant increase or decrease of the dispersion ellipsis. Bearing that in mind that all the targets, if the firing came from that ridge, if I can put it that way, Zarkovica, Srdj, if all the targets around town were lower, underneath, they were below the horizon of targeting. And then taking into account this mild rear slope, we can say that these two elements quite simply preclude the possibility of a significant change. On the one hand, the dispersion was increased a bit. On the other hand, it was increased a little bit, so practically, the dispersion pattern that I gave in the report is what it boils down to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just ask two quick question areas and we'll be finished within a couple minutes, sir. Sir, there was a lot of talk yesterday concerning mortars being artillery versus infantry-type weapons. In approximately 1985 they were switched to being infantry weapons. Even though that change did occur in 1985, which combat arm or branch of the military trained mortar operators?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my experience, from 1985 when the mortars became infantry weapons, up to 1991 when I did my last firing exercise with the cadets from mortars at the school centre, the school centre was served by regular army units, mortar units, because our centre did not have its own units. However, the commanding over these mortar units that served the school centre was done by officers and junior officers that had been students at the centre and to whom I -- whose teacher I had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are those people who were part of the artillery unit? Or were trained by the artillery units, or the artillery branch, probably? Better phrase.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
